#808. Live Tinted’s Founder Shares Her Secret to a "Luminous" Diwali Glow

E! exclusively spoke with Deepica Mutyala, founder of Live Tinted, about how to achieve a "luminous" glow for Diwali, and how she formulates her unique & purposeful products.

Live Tinted made history just over 5 years ago at Ulta Beauty when they became the first South Asian-founded makeup brand to launch there, and recently came together for a special Diwali celebration.

Following her star-studded event, E! spoke exclusively with founder Deepica Mutyala about her partnership with Ulta, the best products to get a luminous Diwali glow, plus her commitment to purposeful formulas and inclusive shade ranges.

Deepica shared, "It's honestly such a full-circle moment! When we launched at Ulta Beauty in 2021 as its first South Asian-founded makeup brand, it was a milestone I never could have imagined growing up. Five years later, we're one of Ulta's fastest-growing prestige cosmetics brands!"

"Hosting one of the beauty industry's largest Diwali celebrations alongside Ulta's leadership this year was incredibly meaningful. The brand's bestselling Hueguard Skin Tint offers buildable, light-to-medium coverage made with skincare actives.

For anyone new to the brand, Deepica says that the bestselling Hueguard ("one sells every two minutes globally" at Ulta, she adds) is what she'd recommend trying out first: "I love it because it combines skincare, SPF 50 protection, and beautiful, natural-looking coverage in one easy step. It's the perfect everyday product and really represents our mission of creating beauty that works for everyone, from the lightest to the deepest skin tones!"

Subtle microshimmers give your skin a naturally radiant and hydrated glow in three different colors: Dawn (rose gold), Dusk (bronze) and Golden Hour (soft gold).

This highly-pigmented gradient bronzer provides a perfectly sunkissed glow, made with hyaluronic acid for hydration and niacinamide to even skin tone.

Of the HUEBEAM Gradient Blushing Bronzer, Deepica added, "I love that it gives you warmth and a beautiful flush of color in one product. My favorite tip is to swirl your brush across the gradient for a seamless, sun-kissed glow, or focus on individual shades to customize your look. Apply it to the high points of your cheeks and blend upward for a naturally lifted finish!"

"That glow comes from feeling happy, confident, and surrounded by the people I love! Diwali has always been such a special time to celebrate family, culture, and new beginnings. Hosting our Diwali celebration with Ulta Beauty this year and seeing so many people from different backgrounds come together was such a beautiful reminder of what makes this holiday so meaningful to me! But if we're talking about an external glow, it has to be our HUEGLOW Liquid Highlighter Drops for that gorgeous, lit-from-within radiance!"

The perfect set to gift or keep for yourself, it includes the trio of HUEGLOW shades: Dawn, Golden Hour and Dusk.

"Everything starts with listening to our community and identifying real gaps in the beauty industry. How do you recommend using the Color Corrector?

#807. Dorgu makes dramatic impact - Man Utd v Aston Villa ratings

Patrick Dorgu rises to head Manchester United's injury-time equaliser in a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

Manchester United fought back from two goals twice to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa as Patrick Dorgu made a dramatic impact off the bench.

But who impressed and who didn't in the Old Trafford epic?

Senne Lammens: One of Man Utd's best performers this season but a calamitous start to this one. First goal went straight through him and he spilled a shot straight from Nicolas Jackson for the second. Went wrong way for penalty too. 4

Diogo Dalot (off 66, Dorgu): Got his body in the right position to close half the goal off for the opener but was in the wrong position to make challenge on Alysson at start of second half to gift Villa a penalty. 4

Leny Yoro: Moved back into the centre, intelligently stepped up to win the ball on halfway, then spoiled good work by attempting a lofted pass when Matheus Cunha wanted it on the ground. Almost headed into his own net in build-up to Villa's fourth goal. 5

Harry Maguire (off 46, Heaven): Managed to clear his head quickly enough to lead United's defence after their shocking start. A doubt pre-match, he went off at half-time. 5

Noussair Mazraoui: Struggled along with many others this season. Asked to push forward, which he seems to find easier for his country but not his club. 4

Youri Tielemans (off 66, Mount): Baited by the Aston Villa fans given his Â£35m summer move from them, but answered in the best way by driving home an equaliser for his first United goal. 6

Kobbie Mainoo: Threatened with a long-range effort and nearly picked out Amad Diallo's run with a precise chipped pass over the visitors defence. 6

Amad Diallo (off 66, Lacey): Kept his place ahead of crowd favourite Shea Lacey but one chase back into his own box showed why, defensively, it made sense. Came close to an equaliser and should have ended an 11-month wait for a goal but Zion Suzuki saved well. 6

Bruno Fernandes: For the second game running, he kept his cool to covert from the spot when the pressure was at its highest. Looked unhappy at the end despite the comeback. 7

Matheus Cunha: Driving run into the visiting box brought a crucial penalty. Curling effort was heading for the corner but turned around post by Suzuki. United's most dangerous attacker. 7

Bryan Mbeumo (off 83, Zirkzee): Did a lot of chasing in the first half to try to pressure the Villa defence into mistakes. 6

Ayden Heaven (on 46, Maguire): Booked for late tackle on Alysson after being introduced at break. 6

Mason Mount (on 66, Tielemans): Hit the bar with first time shot but sliced later effort over. 6

Shea Lacey (on 66, Amad): Tried to create. 6

Patrick Dorgu (on 66 Dalot): What an ending as he changed the outcome of the game with an assist and goal. 8

Joshua Zirkzee (on 83, Mbeumo): Scored in stoppage time and goal proved crucial. 6

Subs not used: Darlow, De Ligt, Andrey Santos, J Fletcher.

Bizarre & thrilling theatre as Carrick's Man Utd future still in limbo

Premier League: Man Utd score twice in stoppage time to draw with Villa but stay in drop zone

Zion Suzuki: Kept busy as the hosts hunted an equaliser. One excellent save from Cunha and a couple when he benefited from a kind rebound, but bad error for United's late equaliser. 5

Victor Lindelof: Found himself under a lot of pressure on a ground he knows so well and turned in an accomplished performance. 7

Taylor Harwood-Bellis: Had to remain concentrated and wasn't faultless but emerged with credit in the bank. 6

Pau Torres: Guided a header over as Villa attacked but biggest task was trying to stop Cunha. As it turned out, a stride too late getting out when Tielemans scored. Couldn't keep United out in the end. 6

Ian Maatsen: Testing day, trying to stop Amad attacking and looking to beat Mazraoui at the other end. Was doing well until the late drama. 7

Alysson (off 71, Barkley): Even the Brazilian must have been a little bit surprised his first-minute shot ended up in the net. His shot created the second and came so close to adding another to his tally after being released by Goretzka. Won the penalty at start of second half too. 8

Boubacar Kamara: Ill-advised attempted tackle on Cunha led to penalty that offered the hosts a way back into the game. Struggled to contain the home attack. 7

John McGinn (off 71, Hemmings): Everything looked so good in the opening minutes but then had to try to ensure Villa didn't fall apart as United fought back. Kept his concentration to score from the spot and created panic with a free-kick. 7

Leon Goretzka (off 78, Mbaye): Tried to relieve pressure on Villa defence as the hosts fought back and drove home Villa's fourth on a crazy day. 7

Johan Manzambi (off 78, Gomes): Not the easiest game for the Swiss international to shine given its general chaotic nature. Tried to get control but no real chance of that. 5

Nicolas Jackson (off 86, Madjo): Alert to snaffle home the rebound after Lammens had spilled McGinn's shot. Not the best performance but much effective than in his Chelsea days. 7

George Hemmings (on 71, McGinn): Came on to shore things up but move didn't work. 5

Ross Barkley (on 71, Alysson): Won't remember ending with fondness. 5

Subs not used: Bizot, Mings, Buendia, Cisse.

#806. Where does Man Utd 4-4 Villa rank among best Premier League games?

Manchester United trailed Aston Villa by two goals after just three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest they had ever been 2-0 down in the Premier League

When Manchester United and Aston Villa served up an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon, it was an instant Premier League classic.

While the match will not define either side's season, it will be remembered for years to come.

In fact, it was only the 29th time in Premier League history both teams had scored four goals each in the same match.

It was not the first time United have been involved in a high-scoring Premier League encounter, either.

Last December, the Red Devils had to settle for a share of the points against Bournemouth after another game where eight goals were shared.

And in Sir Alex Ferguson's final match in charge of United in May 2013, they drew 5-5 with West Brom at The Hawthorns.

But where does Sunday's match rank among the other remarkable matches we have witnessed down the years?

This result played a major factor in the outcome of the title race eventually won by Manchester United

Having blown a 10-point lead at the top of the table, Newcastle's title hopes suffered a major blow as they lost a classic in stoppage time at Anfield despite having led twice.

Sergio Aguero's late winner delivered the most dramatic end to a Premier League title race

In an extraordinary conclusion to the 2011-12 campaign, Manchester City scored twice in stoppage time to beat Queens Park Rangers on the final day and win their first title in 44 years.

Sergio Aguero's famous late winner ensured City pipped rivals Manchester United, who had already won that day, to the trophy on goal difference.

Andrey Arshavin enjoyed his finest night in an Arsenal shirt at Anfield

On another remarkable evening at Anfield, Arsenal's Andrey Arshavin produced a stunning individual display - netting all four goals for the Gunners to deliver a serious blow to Liverpool's title ambitions.

Zirkzee's goal was his first in the Premier League this season

United seemed dead and buried, not once but twice, as they trailed Europa League winners Aston Villa 2-0 and then 4-2 at Old Trafford.

But late strikes from substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and then Patrick Dorgu, deep into stoppage time, may have rescued not only a point, but Michael Carrick's job as United manager.

Cheick Tiote scored a sensational late equaliser for Newcastle

Arsenal were 4-0 up at and cruising at half-time as they looked to chase down league leaders Manchester United.

However, Abou Diaby was then sent off for the Gunners as Newcastle produced a stunning comeback to earn an improbable draw - with Cheick Tiote's thumping 87th-minute strike clinching the point.

Philippe Albert (right) scored a superb chip to round off Newcastle's 5-0 win

With Manchester United having beaten Newcastle to the title the previous season, this felt like payback for Kevin Keegan and his players, who had also suffered a 4-0 reverse to Sir Alex Ferguson's side at Wembley in the Charity Shield just weeks earlier.

David Beckham scored Manchester United's fifth goal

Manchester United staged a magnificent comeback from 3-0 down at the break to overwhelm Tottenham at White Hart Lane.

Dean Richards, Les Ferdinand and Christian Ziege all scored for the hosts but a transformed United hit back through Andy Cole, Laurent Blanc, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Juan Sebastian Veron and David Beckham.

Michael Owen provided the decisive moment for the hosts late on

Michael Owen's winner deep into stoppage time gave Manchester United a dramatic victory in a classic derby at Old Trafford.

The moment prompted Ferguson to set off on an impromptu wild dance along the touchline, while City boss Mark Hughes - whose side had come from behind three times - questioned why the game had gone on for six added minutes rather than the four allocated.

Mark Viduka scored all four goals for Leeds

Liverpool had gone 2-0 up early on with goals from Sami Hyypia and Christian Ziege, but Mark Viduka scored either side of half-time to drag Leeds level.

Vladimir Smicer restored Liverpool's advantage, before two goals in three minutes from former Celtic forward Viduka secured an incredible win for the hosts.

Crystal Palace's late show had huge implications in the title race

Title-chasing Liverpool had just lost to Chelsea at Anfield, but looked set to power themselves back into the race when they took a commanding 3-0 lead at Selhurst Park.

But they squandered that advantage in a chaotic final 11 minutes, leaving Luis Suarez in tears at the final whistle. Man City went on to win the league by two points.

This was another Arsenal v Manchester United match packed with incident

A tight pitch, a packed Highbury and another compelling contest between two of English football's heavyweights.

The Gunners went two goals up courtesy of Nicolas Anelka and Patrick Vieira only for the champions to draw level thanks to two Teddy Sheringham efforts.

But in a season when Arsene Wenger's side were to wrestle the title away from Manchester, David Platt scored the winner.

There were fireworks in the Highbury tunnel before play even got under way

Most people will remember this game because of the fiery exchange between captains Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane in the tunnel before the game, but the 90 minutes itself were just as thrilling.

Vieira opened the scoring for Arsenal before they were pegged back by an Ashley Cole own goal.

Another Gunners legend, Dennis Bergkamp, helped the hosts retake the lead before two goals from a young Cristiano Ronaldo and a delightful John O'Shea chip stunned Arsene Wenger's side.

Chelsea supporters enjoyed dashing the title hopes of their London rivals Tottenham

A match that meant most for a side that wasn't involved - the day that Leicester City were crowned champions will go down in footballing history.

Two first-half goals from Harry Kane and Heung-min Son gave Tottenham hope of chasing the Foxes down at the business end of the season.

But Gary Cahill and Eden Hazard scored to get Jamie Vardy and his Leicester team-mates' party started as tempers flared in the second half of a match dubbed the 'Battle of the Bridge'.

Eli Junior Kroupi's goal rounded off a thrilling evening at Old Trafford

Manchester United and Bournemouth played out at a Premier League classic at Old Trafford last season.

The hosts led three times and thought they had won the game when they scored twice in 129 seconds to turn a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 advantage.

But Eli Junior Kroupi's strike in the 84th minute pegged Ruben Amorim's side back once again as both sides had to settle for a share of the spoils.

A version of this article was first published in December 2025.

#805. Jacob Elordi Debuts Blonde Hair During Date Night With Kendall Jenner

Jacob Elordi ditched his signature brunette locks for a blonde hair transformation, debuting his new look while out for a casual date night with Kendall Jenner Nov. 7.

Keeping up with Jacob Elordi might prove difficult after his latest transformation.

The Wuthering Heights star enjoyed a date night with Kendall Jenner in New York City Nov. 7, where he showed off a new blonde hairdo, as seen in photos obtained by DeuxMoi.

In one snap, Elordi, 29, sat across from Jenner, 31, as the pair enjoyed a few drinks before attending Broadway’s Paranormal Activity. Keeping it low key, the Euphoria alum donned a black long sleeve top and matching beanie.

But it was the tuft of blonde hair peeking out of the accessory that turned heads.

During the outing, Elordi appeared to have ditched his signature brunette locks for a much lighter color, with the dye job also appearing to take up residence on his eyebrows.

Meanwhile, Jenner kept it classy in a black trench coat.

Yet, this wouldn’t be the first time the Kissing Booth alum has rocked a new look in the reality star’s presence. After all, Elordi proved during a Los Angeles lunch outing with Jenner in September that when it comes to growing facial hair, he does amazing, sweetie.

In one snap of the pair leaving a Los Angeles hotspot, Elordi—dressed in an all-black ensemble paired with sunglasses and a backwards hat—showed off an unexpected goatee, which he has since swapped for a clean-shaven look.

And while it remains to be seen whether Elordi’s makeover is tied to a new role, undergoing a dramatic transformation for the big screen is nothing new for the Oscar nominee.

In fact, Guillermo del Toro told E! News last year that Elordi “took around 10 hours every day” to become the Creature in the filmmaker’s 2025 adaptation of Frankenstein, adding that he had “about 42 pieces of makeup, prosthetics. And then he would have to work.”

And it’s safe to say that all the hours Elordi put into the transformation didn’t go unnoticed, with del Toro noting how “he did it all with grace and patience and love.”

But that doesn’t mean the process was an easy one.

“Your skin gets washed out and covered with something new,” Elordi told Netflix’s Tudum last November. “Your face, and its structure, change. Then you put the costume on and there’s leather and furs, and the weight—it’s all real.”

However, it was during those long hours spent in hair and makeup that Elordi underwent an equally significant internal transformation.

“From the moment I got into the makeup trailer [the performance] began, and it was alive,” he explained. “Guillermo said this would be not just a meditation, but a metamorphosis.”

#804. Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool

If a good striker can always get their team out of a hole, Alessia Russo is doing her best to drag Arsenal out of a deep chasm of uncertainty. Her two goals gave the ­under‑pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, some brief respite with a much-needed, albeit still rather unconvincing victory.

Russo’s double took her impressive recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances. Her goals were priceless for an Arsenal team who arrived on Merseyside with just one win in their previous seven Women’s Super League games. They will be relieved to have won after Liverpool posed plenty of problems and the hosts were unhappy about a ­disallowed goal.

Arsenal began the match brightly, with Lisa Baum’s effort deflecting on to the bar and Olivia Smith firing over from a tight angle. They were rewarded when a good move down their right led to Emily Fox’s cross being angled into the net by Russo’s incisive first-time finish.

Liverpool were level six minutes later, though, and from a defensive point of view it was a familiarly exasperating story for Arsenal, who have conceded from simple long balls through the middle ­several times this season.

They exerted very little pressure as Liverpool found Natalia Ramos in space and her direct ball picked out Beata Olsson up front, with the Arsenal centre-backs Steph Catley and Leah Williamson positioned so far apart that they were almost in different time zones, ­playing Olsson onside. Liverpool’s central striker did enough to keep the ball away from Williamson and lash her strike into the bottom corner.

A curling Ramos free-kick was tipped on to the bar by the Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez, before the game’s most contentious moment left Liverpool feeling ­understandably aggrieved. Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net at the far post after ­Arsenal failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann, despite the delivery towards the player having been ­inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side, who looked baffled.

That seemed to wake Arsenal from their slumber, however, and ­Caitlin Foord went close before Russo restored Arsenal’s lead in the final minute of the first half, as her downward header from Baum’s cross was too precise for Khiara Keating to reach. Slegers praised Russo, as she said: “She’s in top form. The two goals are such clean finishes. She picks up really good positions in the box.”

After a very watchable first half for neutrals, the second half was comparatively less entertaining but still tense as Liverpool fought to try to force an equaliser. They almost found it in the 89th minute but Gareth Taylor had his head in his hands in disbelief after Cornelia Kapocs volleyed wide from a glorious, unmarked position in front of goal. Arsenal clung on.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Liverpool are now winless in five league games but their defender Grace Fisk, who signed a new contract on Saturday, said: “There were so many positives. We made them very uncomfortable for large parts of the game. It’s just the bits in both boxes right now that are letting us down.” ­Taylor, Liverpool’s head coach, agreed: “­Performance‑wise, I couldn’t ask for any more from the girls.”

Slegers, who next has a ­daunting trip to face the European champions Barcelona, said: “The way we defended at the end of the game, for our lives, with so much passion and pride for the shirt, that ball wasn’t going to go in.”

Chengdu lost 1-0 to Dalian in their penultimate game of the season

Chengdu Rongcheng lost a fourth successive game to give up a 12-point lead and throw away the Chinese Super League title.

A 3-2 loss on the final day to Shandong Taishan, combined with a 3-1 win for Dalian Yingbo against Tianjin Tiger, meant John Aloisi's side missed out on the Li Guozu trophy.

It was a remarkable finale for Chengdu, who picked up just one point from their last five matches, while Dalian collected 15 from 15.

Both sides finished level on 52 points, but Dalian took the title with a better head-to-head record which included a victory over Chengdu in the penultimate game of the season.

The title-race collapse will go down as one of the worst in football history, especially with the faltering finish from the side led by Australian Aloisi, who had spells at Portsmouth and Coventry City during his playing career.

Kevin Keegan's Newcastle United famously gave up a 12-point lead to Manchester United in 1995-96 to miss out on the Premier League, while the Red Devils also blew a 12-point advantage over Arsenal in the 1997-98 campaign.

Despite their dreadful run of form, the title was still very much in Chengdu's hands going into the final day.

A point would have been enough to crown them champions, but they found themselves 2-0 down within the opening 25 minutes as Raphael Merkies and Guilherme Madruga scored.

Felipe Silva replied, but Cryzan restored Shandong's two-goal lead.

Former Arsenal forward Wellington Silva gave Aloisi's side hope again with 11 minutes left, but they were unable to find the all-important equaliser.

That outcome left Dalian needing a win in front of their own fans to secure a remarkable title triumph.

They were in front inside five minutes through Yang Mingrui, but Xadas levelled with a 50th-minute penalty.

Liao Jintao, though, restored the lead with 20 minutes to go before a close-range strike from Huang Shan in stoppage time sealed the success and the title.

#801. Fan injured after falling through hole in stand

Tromso's Romssa Arena, pictured before a Conference League game against Brighton in August, is 200 miles inside the Arctic Circle

A fan was taken to hospital after a number of Bodo/Glimt supporters fell through a hole in the away stand at Tromso.

The Norwegian top-flight match at Romssa Arena on Sunday was paused just before half-time after Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called for the referee's attention.

Bodo/Glimt press officer Simen Pedersen told the Reuters news agency that "up to five people fell through the stands".

"We stood and bounced to a supporter song, then the floor gave way," Bodo supporter Andrine Moen told local newspaper Verdens Gang, as reported by Reuters.

"It cracked in two in the row in front of us. There were at least two people who fell through the floor, but we don't know how far they fell or how many fell in total."

The remaining Bodo supporters were moved into other parts of the ground before the match resumed.

The match at Tromso's stadium - the northernmost venue in Norway's Eliteserien - was played in heavy rain.

The score was 0-0 at the time of the incident, but Bodo forward Ola Brynhildsen scored twice after the game resumed to give the league leaders a 2-0 win.

Bodo are locked in a title battle with Viking and the Eliteserien season is set to finish in the first week of December.

#800. The palaeo cave art that hid in plain sight for 26,000 years

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Chris Simms is a science writer based in Somerset, UK.

Inscriptions at the Cova de la Font Major cave system in Catalonia in northeastern Spain prompts rethink of prehistoric population and cultural trends. Credit: Vergès Bosch, J. M., Salas-Altès, M./Antiquity

Inscriptions at the Cova de la Font Major cave system in Catalonia in northeastern Spain prompts rethink of prehistoric population and cultural trends. Credit: Vergès Bosch, J. M., Salas-Altès, M./Antiquity

Archaeologists have described hundreds of rock-art engravings dating back around 26,000 years in a cave frequently visited by tourists in Catalonia — a region of northeastern Spain that was thought to be almost devoid of palaeolithic art1. The findings were published in the journal Antiquity on 5 November.

Josep Maria Vergès Bosch, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES-CERCA) in Tarragona, Spain, spotted some prehistoric engravings among more-modern graffiti in the Cova de la Font Major during a planned excavation in 2019.

Vergès and archaeologist Míriam Salas-Altès at IPHES-CERCA studied 280 Palaeolithic art motifs, including 55 animal depictions, from the cave. “The sheer quantity of art discovered at the Cova de la Font Major is exceptional,” says Salas-Altès.

The cave system — made up of more than 3.5 kilometres of underground passageways that have been occupied numerous times during human history — has been open to the public for some seven decades and became a museum in the 1990s.

The drawings were easy to miss. “When you shine a light straight on the engravings, they are really difficult to see, you have to play with light from different directions to see the depressions,” says Salas-Altès.

Researcher Míriam Salas-Altès documents engravings in a tunnel of the cave system. Credit: Josep Maria Vergès/IPHES-CERCA

The etchings include images of animals such as a horse, a bear and an aurochs (the ancestor of domestic cattle), as well as myriad swirling lines. A handful of the engravings reveal how the artists used “natural lines or fissures in the walls”, says Salas-Altès. For example, “one is used to represent the ground under a horse”.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03585-z

Vergès Bosch, J. M. & Salas-Altès, M. Antiquity https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2026.10447 (2027).

#799. Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid

They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side.

At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos.

“The lesson is that when you can finish it, you have to,” Jan Oblak said afterwards but there was no real reproach. The Atlético goalkeeper insisted that his team would do it again, and that they weren’t going to give up. After seven successive wins, they lost but they had certainly competed; another lesson might be that both of these teams are in the title race, not just Barcelona. Simeone Sr might agree with his son that in the first half the plan had been executed to “perfection”. He might also concede that in the second they found the ball taken from them.

Atlético flew into this, fuelled by the noise. They did more inside three minutes than in 90 against Bayern Munich in midweek. A superb clearance from Pau Cubarsí denied them in the first minute. Álex Baena curled wide in the second. And they forced a corner in the third. Barcelona were overwhelmed and exposed, unable to settle, and Diego Simeone’s side could sense it.

They could see it too, all that space behind the visiting defence, and soon Koke released Julián Álvarez into it. He had a long way to run and a long time to think. Perhaps too long. Was this the moment for the striker who had wanted to join Barcelona in the summer but been forced to stay, redemption and forgiveness laid before him? As he raced into the area, he opted to go round Joan García but the goalkeeper stretched and just about Álvarez was facing the goal again, sufficient Barcelona players had recovered to clear.

A Norwegian top-tier match between Tromso and Bodø/Glimt was interrupted yesterday when a panel in the away fans’ stand gave way, sending some supporters tumbling below. Norwegian broadcaster NRK said several Bodø/Glimt supporters fell through, with four receiving medical attention including one who was hospitalised. The game at Tromso’s stadium later resumed after the incident in the 41st minute, with Bodø/Glimt going on to win 2-0. “Four people were confirmed to be involved, and one of them has been taken to the hospital,” a Tromso statement said. The family of the hospitalised man told NRK that he had sustained fractured ribs.

In Serie A, Inter brought Como crashing down to earth as first-half goals from Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram earned them a 2-0 home win. Como continued their remarkable debut season in Europe on Wednesday by thrashing Lens 9-1, but Cesc Fabregas’ side turned in a lacklustre display at San Siro as their six-game winning run in all competitions was halted. The victory means Inter are only one point behind leaders Lazio, who drew 1-1 away to Napoli. The Rome side remain unbeaten after nine matches, despite an own goal from Alfonso Pedraza in the second half. That came after Davide Frattesi had scored a first-half goal to put the visitors ahead. Milan are up to fourth place after beating Genoa 2-1, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scoring the goals inside the first 20 minutes. Equalisers from Nick Woltemade and Gleison Bremer earned Juventus a 2-2 draw against Fiorentina.

Lille remain two points behind Ligue 1 leaders Paris Saint-Germain after beating Rennes 2-1, while Monaco were denied victory against Le Mans after a 90th-minute equaliser from Erwan Colas. Lens’ week did not improve, with Marseille claiming a late winner in a 2-1 victory. In the Bundesliga, Freiburg climbed to third with a 2-0 win against struggling Union Berlin, while Bayer Leverkusen were 2-1 winners away at Cologne.

Not for long. From the corner, Marc Pubill thudded a header against the bar and although Barcelona did the same at the other end when Lamine Yamal and Pedri combined for the latter to shoot, Atlético soon had the lead. It started with a superb crossfield ball to open up the right wing where Marcos Llorente and Lee Kang-in worked the space for the Korean to guide a pass to Álvarez coming in off the other wing. He immediately returned it across the face of the box where Simeone Jr was thundering in at top speed, which is the speed he always runs at. From seven yards, without breaking his frantic stride, he scored.

The Metropolitano erupted. They had only been playing 10 minutes but this was no more than Atlético deserved and they kept on coming back for more. Every time they changed the direction of play, space yawned before them. Baena was going at Barcelona on the left, Alejandro Grimaldo joining him. Lee did the same on the right, Llorente with him. Pablo Barrios was taking a grip in the middle. As for Simeone, he was everywhere, screeching about the pitch like a cartoon whirlwind, arms and legs occasionally visible sticking out of a wild dust cloud. As for Álvarez, he moved smartly through the chaos.

Álvarez might have added a goal to his assist, his shot escaping under García and almost over the line. He also set up a wonderful opportunity for David Hancko, alone in front of goal, but the effort slipped just wide. Then Lee’s shot was stopped by García.

Barcelona could be grateful the lead was only one still. Would be, in fact. They were almost level on half an hour when Lamine Yamal slipped in – the angle was tight and from close range he hit the side-netting – and on 45 minutes, they were level. There was still a vulnerability when Atlético leapt out, but Barcelona had begun to get a bit of the ball, edging their way into the game and equalising it too. Pedri drove at the Atlético defence, neat footwork taking him through a tight passageway to find Fermín. There was fortune in the deflection off Pubill but the finish was superb.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Half-time came as a reset; with the storm seen out and Frenkie de Jong introduced, Barcelona started the second period better. Pushing Atlético back, the press better applied now, the ball was moved with more precision and more comfort too. Twice Lamine Yamal let fly and twice Pubill had to intercept as Barcelona began to impose.

And yet the best opportunity in those opening minutes fell to Álvarez on 55. Running through, he lifted his shot over García and over the bar, his shot at redemption gone and replaced by frustration and renewed doubts instead. Baena would be played in by Álvarez too but, as if shocked to find the ball landing at his feet all alone by the far post, he hesitated. Unsure what to do, his attempt at scooping the ball up to Alexander Sørloth didn’t come off.

Tiredness afforded Barcelona a little more time and space now, the threat from Atlético far less insistent while theirs increased: by fulltime they would have racked up 19 shots. And when Fermín made yet another sharp, darting run on 66 minutes, Lamine Yamal played a clever, perfectly weighted pass into the area for him to cut the shot past Oblak for his second of the night, his eighth of the season.

It wasn’t over, the feeling that the olés from the visiting fans were premature and tempting fate reinforced when Pubill ran through and found Álvarez, whose deflected shot looped over. Yet Flick’s side had this where they wanted it, his changes underlining that the priority now was a control which they exercised to the end, Atlético’s fire put out. At the whistle, they embraced, exhausted as an ovation went round. They had been in a fight and there will be more to come, but Barcelona were still standing top at the end of it.

#798. Leeds condemn racist abuse of Bogle after Tel incident

Jayden Bogle has scored one goal for Leeds United this season and played in all 10 of their Premier League matches so far

Leeds United have condemned the "disgusting" online racist abuse directed towards defender Jayden Bogle following Saturday's 1-0 win against Tottenham.

The 26-year-old Leeds defender was targeted after he escaped punishment for a first-half tackle on Mathys Tel that led to the Spurs forward hobbling off.

The full-back caught the back of Tel's ankle with his studs but referee John Brooks decided not to punish him following a lengthy video assistant referee review.

Tottenham are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send Bogle off and will write to refereeing body Pro Ref to seek an explanation.

Leeds said they had been "appalled" by the racist abuse posted on social media about Bogle, adding it condemned the behaviour "in the strongest possible terms".

"There is no place for racism in football or society," a club statement read.

"The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them."

Tottenham set to complain to Pro Ref after Bogle escapes red card

Okafor downs Tottenham to earn Leeds first win since September

Bogle reportedly disabled comments on his Instagram account on Saturday after Leeds' win at Elland Road.

On Sunday, Leeds published a selection of messages Bogle had received - with his permission - to highlight their severity.

"Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time," Leeds added.

"Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse."

Tottenham also released a statement, external on Sunday saying the club had been "disgusted" by the abuse suffered by Bogle and have offered their support in identifying those responsible.

"We will pursue every available avenue to ensure they are identified and face the full consequences of their actions," read the statement.

"Regardless of club allegiances and on-pitch results, no-one should ever stand alone in the face of this."

It is not the first time this year that Tottenham have had a player, or an opposition player, suffer online racist abuse after a Premier League game.

Tottenham defender Kevin Danso was targeted by "vile" abuse in April, the weekend after Sunderland's Brian Brobbey had been the subject of racist abuse following an incident in a match against Spurs.

That followed four incidents in February over the same weekend, when Burnley midfielder Hannibal Mejbri, Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana, Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare and Sunderland winger Romaine Mundle were all targeted, which led to a police investigation.

Anti-discrimination group Kick It Out said in April that reports of online abuse were at record levels, increasing by a third compared to the previous season.

At that time, UK Football Policing Unit deputy director Mike Ankers told BBC Radio 5 Live that it had seen an increase of about 115% in the number of reports of online abuse.

#797. Who Is Justin Timberlake's "What Goes Around...Comes Around" About?

Justin Timberlake dispelled the longtime rumor that his 2006 hit “What Goes Around…Comes Around” is about his ex Britney Spears, revealing the real inspiration behind the track.

What goes around comes all the way back around 20 years later.

Nearly two decades after Justin Timberlake released his 2006 single “What Goes Around…Comes Around,” the Grammy winner set the record straight on the longtime speculation that the track was inspired by his breakup with Britney Spears.

“Maybe I should dispel a rumor at this point, which has gone around forever,” the 45-year-old shared on a Nov. 5 episode of Complex’s Re-Rank podcast. “It’s not a personal story from mine.”

In fact, Timberlake—who famously dated Spears from 1999 to 2002—said the song, which follows a woman who betrays her partner, before karma results in her facing the same fate,  is “actually a personal story from a friend” that he asked to use as inspiration for the track.

“He was just going through it, and he was telling me what had happened,” he recalled. “I said, ‘Do you mind if I write about this?’ And I quote, my friend said, ‘Yeah, torch that b--ch. What goes around comes around.’”

“And I was like, ‘I have to go. Thank you,’” Timberlake joked while pretending like he was on a phone. “He was like, ‘What?’ I was like, ‘I got it.’”

After ending the call with his friend, the “SexyBack” singer couldn’t stop the feeling of inspiration and immediately began writing.

“I hung up the phone,” Timberlake recalled. “I had the idea. I just went in and again, this song was written in, I mean, damn near 20 minutes. It was just flowing.”

He continued, “The interlude that goes with it, and then you put the video with it—there’s a 10-minute video we shot for it—this just hit on all cylinders for me.”

Because of this, the “Mirrors” artist noted that he would rank “What Goes Around…Comes Around”—the third single from his second album FutureSex/LoveSounds—as “one or two” if they were “ranking the bangers” from his discography. (He ultimately slotted it at No. 1.)

While Timberlake has now shared the way it was really going down when he wrote the hit, fans have long speculated that the Grammy-winning track was a sequel to his 2002 single “Cry Me a River,” which has also been believed to be about Spears.

After all, not only was the song released eight months after his split from Spears, but he also cast her lookalike in the music video.

And similar to “What Goes Around…Comes Around,” the lyrics quickly poured out of Timberlake.

“I wrote that song in about 10 minutes, five to 10 minutes,” he shared, confirming that he recorded “every vocal” within less than two hours.

#796. Evanilson ignites eighth straight Bournemouth win at blundering Ipswich

Marco Rose paid tribute to his Bournemouth side after a hard‑fought 2-1 victory at Ipswich equalled the club’s record of eight consecutive wins.

Evanilson got the ball rolling after five minutes, scoring for a fifth successive Premier League match. With seven goals this season, he has already beaten his tally from the whole of last season.

His latest was a gift from the Ipswich goalkeeper, Christian Walton, who tried and failed to dribble past ­him in the area, and Bournemouth went two up after 27 seconds of the second half when Leif Davis could only deflect Ryan Christie’s strike into his own net.

Lewis Cook tripped Abdoul ­Ouattara in the area to provide the hosts with a lifeline and Jack Clarke scored the penalty with 17 minutes left to set up a grandstand finish at Portman Road.

However, Bournemouth stood firm to make it eight wins in a row and match the record set under Eddie Howe in 2012-13, a season which ended with promotion from League One.

Speaking after a win which came three days after a victorious journey to Sparta Prague, Rose said: “I am pleased with the first 70 minutes because we went two up and I didn’t feel like we struggled or can get any problems, but it’s [the] Premier League and one goal changed the momentum of the game.

“That is why I am much more pleased with the last 20 minutes. We suffered but we did it together.”

A slow start last month at Chelsea proved costly for Bournemouth, and even in last weekend’s 2-0 home win against Leeds the visitors had an effort ruled out after 11 minutes. That made goals at the start of each half particularly sweet for Rose.

“Last week I said we start slow and this week I said we start quite quick and score an early goal. I am a magician!” the German said with a smile. “No, we know we have to be ready in this league. We played Chelsea four weeks ago and we were two down after three minutes. That’s why we learned and always good to score an early goal.

“We were sharp, we were good and that’s what I really appreciate. I said before this week that it’s going to be really demanding for a team that is not used to have this kind of [­European] situation.”

Julio Enciso went close late on with two free‑kicks, but this defeat means Ipswich have only won one of their last seven in all competitions.

Gary O’Neil, their manager, said: “[We are] gutted with the result, firstly, because it’s what we are here for and probably performance-wise not much in it. To lose a football match you’ve not been outclassed in is hard to take. But if you give the ball to the opposition No 9 twice, it’s going to be difficult and that was the story of the game really.

“It’s the level so we have to find a way of not only being competitive in games, but can we now find a way to make sure these Hull [a 2-2 draw] and Bournemouth performances are four points and not one.”

#793. Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?

The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow has increasingly relied on a so-called shadow fleet to bypass Western sanctions and transport its oil around the world.

Other heavily sanctioned countries, including Iran and Venezuela, have also been accused of using such vessels to export petroleum products.

These tankers often rely on deceptive practices like turning off their location transponders to evade detection and conceal the cargo's true origins or destinations.

The fleet, which consists largely of aging, uninsured and poorly maintained tankers, has raised widespread concern across the shipping industry. Yet it has expanded rapidly in recent years and now accounts for nearly 19% of global oil tanker capacity, according to estimates by financial intelligence firm S&P Global.

"The shadow fleet is a scourge," Elisabeth Braw, senior fellow at the think tank Atlantic Council, said, adding that "it is in nobody's interest" to have these ships sailing around in the world's oceans.

She pointed out that these tankers undermine the maritime order and increase the risk of accidents and environmental damage.

"Every country should use its leverage with Russia to ask it not to use the fleet," she told DW, noting that ultimately all countries suffer the consequences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

To clamp down on the fleet and curb Russia's oil export revenues, the United States and European countries have stepped up efforts to intercept tankers accused of violating sanctions.

The Trump administration, however, is reportedly considering lifting sanctions on some shadow fleet vessels and allowing them to transport oil that is not subject to sanctions.

A US official told Reuters earlier this month that the move was intended to ease record-high global freight rates.

Lifting sanctions on the shadow fleet "would decrease the effectiveness of the sanctions regime overall," said Michael Carpenter, senior fellow for Transatlantic Affairs at the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS). Such a move "rewards the aggressor and helps Moscow gain revenues to continue attacking Ukraine," he told DW.

"This is the exact opposite of what the US should be doing if it wants to end the war."

Carpenter, who previously served as US ambassador to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said any sanctions relief would also put the US and the EU "strategically at odds with each other, with the EU clearly backing Ukraine and the US increasingly supporting Russia's financial goals."

This view is shared by Ben Harris, vice president and director of Economic Studies at the Brookings Institution.

Lifting sanctions on shadow fleet tankers would "make it substantially easier for Russia to trade its oil at market rates," he said, pointing out that it would "improve its government finances since so much revenue is tied to energy markets."

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, however, rejected suggestions that the US was removing sanctions from shadow fleet tankers.

"We are converting dark tankers to legitimate tankers," Bloomberg quoted Wright as saying last week. "There is no removing of sanctions," he stressed, adding that the US government was working with investors who buy idle sanctioned tankers, refurbish them and use them to transport oil that is not subject to sanctions.

"We're going to move some of the ships from what I call the 'bad-guy fleet' to the 'good-guy fleet,'" Wright said. "They will not carry sanctioned oil anymore."

The US government has yet to unveil a detailed plan for shadow fleet tankers.

The proposal follows a deal that US President Donald Trump struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin this month to allow sales of Russian diesel onto global markets.

The agreement was seen as part of Trump's efforts to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3.

The US president also waived broad new sanctions on Russia authorized by ​a recent legislation, which targeted Moscow's energy revenues and threatened tariffs against the world's largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas.

The decision was sharply criticized by Ukraine and its European allies over concerns that it could undermine the credibility of sanctions and weaken Western economic pressure on Moscow.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Harris said that "the US sanctions carry outsized weight because of the threat [for countries and businesses] of being cut off from the US financial system."

If the US steps away from its sanctions on the shadow fleet, he argued, "the responsibility shifts to European policymakers." But they have "less effective options because of the diminished threat of severing financial ties."

Still, the expert stressed that Europe has some tools, pointing to the continent's key role in global shipping and insurance services.

"They can implement measures demanding that tankers carry legitimate and established insurance when traveling through their waters," he said, noting that it "would mean that many shadow fleet tankers could not in practice legally transport Russian oil."

Harris added that European policymakers could also pressure countries worldwide to better regulate the tankers flying their flags.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carpenter said even if US eases some restrictions, the EU will have no choice but to continue enforcing its sanctions on these vessels.

"The vast majority of the shadow fleet traverses the Baltic Sea and exits it via the Danish Strait," he noted, adding that the EU is "uniquely positioned to board and inspect vessels moving through this key chokepoint."

But Russia has threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for interdicting and seizing Russian vessels suspected of being part of the shadow fleet.

And without US backing, Carpenter said, "it will be harder for EU countries to take on the burdens and risks of sanctions enforcement."

Braw echoed this view, saying that Ukraine's European allies will have to remain united and continue working closely with partners such as Japan, Australia and Canada. Nevertheless, she stressed that what they can achieve on their own "is far less than what they can achieve if the US is part of the team."

#792. Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise

Falkirk raced into a 4-0 half-time lead away to Hearts

In the space of a week Falkirk have beaten defending champions Celtic and become the first team to get the better of Hearts in a Scottish Premiership match at Tynecastle in 19 months, scoring a combined seven goals in the process.

The 5-2 success in Edinburgh was their fifth successive victory and takes John McGlynn's side up to third place.

A month ago, the concession of an added time goal to Dundee left them 11th, only a point off the bottom of the table.

"It's striking a balance without getting carried away and not playing it down too much," McGlynn told BBC Scotland.

"Winning five games in a row, you've obviously got something about you. We want it to continue because we're enjoying this.

"But we're only 13 games in. There's a long way to go, so we've got to keep our feet on the ground and enjoy seeing our team third in the league."

The 64-year-old earned plaudits aplenty last season for guiding Falkirk to sixth on their return to the top flight after overseeing consecutive promotions.

Liam Henderson, who scored the sublime fourth goal against Hearts, was with the Bairns in those League One days, as were Brad Spencer and Ethan Ross.

Unused substitutes Finn Yeats and Ross MacIver have been on the journey with McGlynn too, as has Leon McCann, who missed out through injury.

"We've got a good team spirit, a togetherness, and a will to work hard for your team-mates," said centre-half Henderson. "We now have a ruthlessness up front as well.

"The manager is massive to us. His knowledge, his detail. He is so detailed in everything he does.

"We're breaking records this season and creating some history. A lot of pundits and fans were saying that we weren't the team we were last year."

There is truth to that. While some of the old guard remain, there was a huge squad turnover in the summer.

Calvin Miller went to Hearts, Dylan Tait is now the skipper at Dundee United and Barney Stewart, who scored 10 goals between January and May, was sold to West Bromwich Albion for a club record fee.

Loan players Filip Lissah, Ben Broggio, Henry Cartwright, Kyrell Wilson, Ethan Williams and Louie Marsh said their goodbyes.

John McGlynn has taken maximum points from two games against his old team Hearts this season

McGlynn brought in a whopping 17 new faces, with Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames and Jacob Murrell, who all scored against Hearts, arriving weeks after the campaign had kicked off.

Murrell, 22, picked up the SPFL player of the month award for October and his Tynecastle double takes his tally to seven, making him joint-top scorer in the division.

"They look at what kind of player fits into the team and when the player arrives, they know what they're getting," said former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart in praise of Falkirk's scouting.

Meanwhile, former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan highlighted captain Spencer as the "heartbeat" of the team.

"You need a guy like him in there to really set the standards," Allan said of the 30-year-old midfielder, who followed McGlynn from Raith Rovers.

"When he is in the team, there is a real control from Falkirk, especially in the middle.

"They've added a steeliness to the team too, it's not always total football this year. They are able to do the dirty side of the game now and roll up the sleeves when they have to."

McGlynn is very much the unassuming star of the show though.

"He is a manager who is totally comfortable in his own skin now," said Stewart.

"He exudes confidence. Perhaps before he was considered a bit of an unfashionable manager. I mean in terms of stature, and not in what he's doing on the park.

"The perception of him continues to get better and better.

"I don't want to be disrespectful to Falkirk, but I would not be surprised, if, when one or two of the bigger jobs start coming up, rather than being an outsider, I think he will be right in the hunt for some of those."

As things stand, almost any move away from Falkirk would be a step down the league.

#791. Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second

Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal.

Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex ­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them.

If Pascal Gross, scorer of a perfectly hit penalty, attempted to dampen expectations of a title challenge, his manager, Fabian Hürzeler, allowed fans to dream. “They should always be excited, it’s our job to make them excited,” he said.

A successful return to the Amex Stadium following five Brighton away trips, more than 5,000 miles on the road including victories at ­Manchester City and Getafe over the past two outings. Brentford returned to a stadium where they have never won in the Premier League. Normal service was duly resumed, any Brighton negatives coming in a failure to add to their first-half goals.

An up-and-under straight from the kick-off was a rare Brentford foray into the Brighton box. Bart Verburggen catching it on the full prefaced an easy afternoon for the Brighton goalkeeper. There are many further dimensions to ­Hürzeler’s team. Last week Paul Scholes, an unlikely ­progressive, declared himself an admirer of a “level of ­coaching” he suggested is ­unsurpassed in ­English football. “The one thing that is non‑negotiable is to always put the team first,” Hürzeler said.

Diego Gómez’s opener was not as spectacular as the halfway-line goal of the season against Crystal Palace but a beauty nonetheless. Caressing the ball first with his left and then with his right, he laid up a thrash past Caoimhín Kelleher. Its trajectory was unerring, unstoppable. Hürzeler revealed: “Yesterday, he changed to shooting with [his] left foot … I couldn’t see him scoring with his left foot. I asked him after where this quality came from.”

The path to a commanding win opened up. Igor Thiago did not last many ­minutes beyond his failed attempt to lob ­Verburggen. Scuffling in midfield with Chema Andrés, his shove was first ruled a yellow by the referee, Michael Oliver. In stepped the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell: “violent conduct” and “with force” was the verdict from Stockley Park.

Afterwards, Andrews was ­visibly unhappy: “We’ve lost two games and both when down to 10 men. So we need to analyse ourselves first. In both scenarios we can do better. In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation.”

Infact, both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were dismissed against Liverpool, and if Andrews rues such lapses of discipline he was more unhappy at the initial decision’s video-assisted overturn: “The game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like.”

Straying beyond the confines of his technical area in a manner likely to add him to Mikel Arteta’s “massive storage of images” of such breaches, Andrews asked his team to dig deep but Brighton’s dominance of possession became near-total.

Luka Vuskovic, ­serving ­previously as a deep-lying playmaker, won the penalty. Keane Lewis-Potter’s ­panicked response to a physical 18-yard box mismatch was to snatch at the ­Croatian’s shirt. Gross’s penalty was struck as truly as Gómez’s goal. “We need to be cuter,” Andrews said. “I take real pride in the way we defend set pieces and we need to do better because that wasn’t good.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Andrews’s half-time ­adjustments, bringing on Yarmolyuk and Nathan Collins, was an attempt to protect Brentford’s goal difference. Brighton continued to pile on pressure, their ­possession share reaching beyond 75%. A set piece became Brentford’s sole route back, though Mathias Jensen’s diagonal into ­Verbruggen’s hands would not have passed muster in rugby’s Nations Championship.

Ironic cheers from the away end came when Brentford won a corner, and then another – rare excitement at Brighton’s defenders being asked to do something other than build an attack. The visitors’ fighting spirit at least sustained, though threatened to spill over. When Kevin Schade shoved ­Vuskovic to the ground by the touchline, another red card was a possibility, only for Oliver and Attwell to rule a yellow as sufficient this time.

Brighton’s push for honours and further horizons will require more than spectacular goals. “You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not ­getting carried away yet,” Gross said. “Every game we have to suffer a lot.”

Hürzeler, like Andrews constantly straying beyond the confines of his technical area, does not countenance any let-ups. When Brighton meet the unstinting demands of their coach, so many are left in their wing mirrors.

#790. Why Love Is Blind's Lauren Speed Thinks Her Engagement Ring Was Fake

Lauren Speed—who met and married husband Cameron Hamilton on season one of Love Is Blind—revealed what made her believe her engagement ring from production was fake: “I was heartbroken."

Lauren Speed is pods-tive that her initial engagement ring was a knockoff.

The Love Is Blind alum—who wed husband Cameron Hamilton during season one of the Netflix show—revealed why she thinks the engagement ring production provided for the couple was fake.

“I think they got real rings now, but mine was not,” Speed said on a recent episode of Cam Newton’s eponymous podcast. “The diamond fell out and turned green when I got in the pool.”

“I was heartbroken,” she added, “but now I think they have a jewelry partner, so they get real rings now.”

In addition to the couple’s engagement rings, Netflix also foots the bill for the brides’ wedding dresses, the wedding ceremonies and gives the contestants stipends for participating on the show, with Speed sharing that she and Hamilton received about $700 a week for their time filming the reality dating series.

And while the show’s participants can certainly clink their metallic wine glasses to that, the series’ creator Chris Coelen previously shed light on production’s bling budget, revealing that while all the couples' selected engagement rings have different prices, "it's generally in that $3,500 to $5,000 range...with some variations.”

And for anyone hoping for something a bit more extravagant?

"If they want to upgrade their rings, they're welcome to do that," Coelen continued to Entertainment Weekly in 2025. "We have nothing to do with that. We give them the rings, they do what they want."

Though it seems times have changed since Speed, 38, and Hamilton, 36, met and married while filming Love Is Blind in 2018, their bond continues to grow in the right direction.

In fact, the pair welcomed their first baby together, a boy named Ezra William Hamilton, last October following years of fertility struggles.

"To God be the GLORY!" Speed wrote on Instagram at the time, sharing that he arrived "a little earlier than planned, but perfectly on God’s time."

And while the path hasn’t been easy, the influencer would do it all again sight unseen for the life she lives today, noting how she was “healing, resting, and soaking up all the love."

Keep reading for more Love Is Blind secrets…

1. Are contestants paid to be on Love Is Blind? Former star Matthew Duliba said they are paid $5,000 to appear on the pod period of the show.

The real money is made in sponsorships afterward, as season two alums Deepti Vempati and Natalie Lee said they each made about $500,000 as influencers in under two years after their episodes aired in 2022.

2. Where do the cast members sleep while in the pods? According to Netflix, the contestants slept on cot beds in trailers next to the lounges during season one, but for season two they upgraded to hotel rooms to be more comfortable. They're escorted to and from their rooms by staff so they can't secretly see anyone.

"You're actually at a hotel," season four's Micah Lussier shared on TikTok in 2025. "That's where you're staying, and then the pods that you see is a set, so think of a big studio, and then the bathrooms are outside in trailers."

3. The reality stars don't get access to their phones starting in the pods until after they're back from their tropical vacation portion of filming.

Shayne Jansen shared of their vacations, "You don't have your phone or anything on you."

4. The pods portion of the experiment lasts about 10 days, with 40-50 hopeful singles serving as the initial cast. But over the course of the process, some singles are let go.

"There was a certain point where we did a whittling down of people just to focus internally on the people who were really connecting, to allow them more time," Love Is Blind creator Chris Coelen told E! News. "We ended up having maybe 20-25 people in the pods at that point."

5. The first dates between all of the singles were set up speed-dating style rotation, with everyone spending eight to 10 minutes with each person of the opposite sex. From then on, there were no limitations put on who you could talk to, when you could talk to them and for how long, as long as a production intermediary set it up as they were unable to communicate with each other outside of the pods.

6. According to Sal Perez from season two, the singles are given "talking points" and "questions" before heading into their dates, but they don't have to use them.

"There were kind of topics for the day," Kyle Abrams added in an interview with E! News. "It was good if there was a lull in conversation, you just refer to the little notebook and you can drum up conversation."

That being said, the show is far from scripted. As contestant Kelly Chase told Business Insider, "Although it might sound unbelievable (trust me, it was hard to believe myself), the show wasn't scripted for the cast."

7. As for what they eat on set? Kelly said that was one of the aspects of filming she enjoyed most, explaining that contestants are offered a wide range of options while in the pods.

"During the first 10 days of filming," she said, "we could choose from catered food that included options like grilled fish, chicken, steak, vegetables, pasta, rice, and fruit."

8. All the proposals happen on the same day, though some are shown earlier in the episodes to avoid watching them all back-to-back.

“Everyone gets engaged on that one day. And then the next day is the big reveal day," Kelly said, per Cosmo. "And then the couples separate and go back through their own door. You meet them [your partner] for 15 minutes—the person you just got engaged to—and then you don’t see them again for a few days. It’s crazy."

9. Where do the engagement rings come from?

"We supply them with the rings, and at that point, those rings are theirs," the creator told Entertainment Weekly in 2025. "They never have to give them back if things don't work out. They're their rings. And if they want to say that they paid for them, then that's up to them. They can say whatever they want."

10. Hosts Vanessa Lachey and Nick Lachey are no longer allowed to be at the reveals.

"We all used to be at the reveal," Vanessa told Parade in 2025. "So when they would come out on the red carpet, it was me, it was Nick, we had like the glam girls there, we had costume design, we had audio. We had everybody standing there."

But it ended up being "probably 50 people" in the room, which detracted from the romance.

"It got to a point where it got too loud," Vanessa added. "After that, they were like, 'No more people at the reveal. Just the cameras and the couple. This is their moment.'"

11. Hoping to see a few proposals, producers were not expecting more than five couples to get engaged in season one. So when two other couples (in addition to the six the show chose to follow) also ended the pod portion with an engagement, producers ultimately couldn't continue filming their journey.

"We felt like we wanted to tell diverse stories frankly," Coelen reasoned. "We weren't sure where the stories were going to go, everybody felt like they truly found the person they wanted to spend their life with and we had an abundance of story...we just didn't have time in the show to follow them, which is incredible to me."

12. One of those engaged couples was Rory Newbrough, who was often seen giving advice to the other men, and Danielle Drouin. They spent a week together in Miami as the other engaged couples went to Mexico to continue filming. But soon after they returned to Atlanta, they had a "very amicable" breakup when Danielle realized she still had feelings for another cast member, Matt Thomas. "She ended up wanting to pursue that," Rory explained to People. Danielle and Matt ultimately didn't last either.

13. The other unaired season one engagement was between Westley Baer, who was briefly shown discussing dating as a shorter man, and Lexie Skipper. Despite not continuing with the show, they dated for three months back in Atlanta. But Westley revealed to People that his career change caused their split. "I made a crazy decision to sell everything I owned, and I moved to Asia," he said.

Two season two couples—Caitlin McKee and Joey Miller and Kara Williams and Jason Beaumont—also got engaged, but didn't have their journeys filmed.

14. Are constants allowed to talk when there's not cameras around?

"In the pod stage, the answer is no," Micah said. "There's always cameras rolling in those pods. And when you're in the lounge, they don't want people talking if there's not cameras rolling, so it will be quiet on set. And that is because if you're talking about stuff, they can miss part of the storyline."

She said the experience in Mexico is similar.

"You won't fly together, you won't do anything off camera until they leave you alone in that room that first night," she said. "So, that's the first time that you get a talk off-camera."

But when they go home, there's more freedom to speak without being filmed.

"You have scheduled filming days, like every other day," she explained. "So of course, you get a ton of time off camera to get to know each other without them in your face."

"They pay for the dress," Micah said of the production team. "I remember when we went there were some dresses that were included and part of the budget, and we could choose from those. And there's a lot to choose from."

However, they also "had the option" to "upgrade" to a more expensive dress that they paid for. The season four star added, "To my knowledge, no one ever did that."

16. As for who paid for the weddings, a Netflix spokesperson revealed to Women's Health that production "supplies some of the basics, but because these are their real weddings, it's up to them as to how to spend their money." So the couples likely did have to cover some expense if they went over budget.

17. Despite some skepticism from viewers, the marriages are legit, with season one's Lauren Speed telling Refinery29, "This is a real legally binding marriage. This is not for TV. This is our life."

18. It's not random who goes first on the alter saying "I do" or "I don't," with Micah saying the production crew determines who goes first.

"It's not the officiant who decides," Micah revealed. "In my opinion, they will ask whoever they think is more likely to say 'yes' to go first, because then they get a two [person] answer."

Otherwise, she noted, "you don't have that chance of seeing the first person say 'yes' and having that shock."

19. So were the cast members obligated to make it to the altar? According to Coelen, they were not. "They certainly could choose to do whatever they wanted to do," he told E! News of the wedding day decision-making process. "Again, being there on the wedding day, I personally, knowing these people and their stories, I didn't know what was going to happen."

20. Then why do people wait until the altar to decide if they're going to say yes or no? While contestants aren't required to go through with the wedding day, there's a reason many do, even if they ultimately say no.

"In my experience, it wasn't like you have to get to the altar, like you must get to the altar," Micah shared on TikTok. "It was moreso being a part of the entire experience. The whole point of Love Is Blind is It's an experiment. And you wouldn't know if it's going to work or not unless you do the whole thing. So that was the thought process there."

21. Why do so few couples say “I do"? After only one pair of contestants tied the knot in season eight, Love Is Blind executive producer Ally Simpson provided insight into why it’s getting more rare for couples to make it past the altar, admitting that social media has made it challenging to recruit “nice men” for the experiment. She also noted that former contestant Chelsea Griffin joined the casting team to help mitigate the issue.

22. There were rumors online that Mark Cuevas, the youngest single man in the inaugural season, secretly had a girlfriend when he was on the show, which he later denied.

"I did not have a girlfriend the whole time," he said on the Be There in Five podcast. "I was single before [going on the show]. Now, being a single man, you're single, you're doing your thing. I'd never had a girlfriend before. Where was the time to be in a relationship during the experience?"

23. According to Kelly and Kenny Barnes, they never had any plans to actually get married at the end of filming season one. "We were adamant about we're not going to get married," Kenny told People. "And really, the engagement was just to extend the experiment. And we were both committed to that." And Kelly believed they were "going to continue dating, because that was communicated between us." That was until Kenny admitted on the wedding day he was not "emotionally available" to do so. "I felt very rejected," she admitted. "Like, 'That wasn't the plan. What the heck?'"

24. Jessica Batten, LIB season one's most polarizing cast member, claimed in an interview that she tried to quit the show but wasn't allowed to.

"I mean, I had to stay," she told EW. "I definitely had a conversation about leaving and I wasn't able to do that. My dog got sick too, and almost died during the show, I had so much other stuff going on."

She continued, "It was really frustrating because I kind of knew [Mark and I] weren't going to get there. I definitely had some conversations and attempted to leave, but I wasn't able to."

25. The season one weddings were actually filmed in the fall of 2018, meaning the two couples—Lauren and Cameron Hamilton, and Amber Pike and Matt Barnett—who actually decided to get married had to keep their relationships secret for 18 months before the show premiered.

26. Love Is Blind could go on and on for years, with Coelen telling E! News, "I'm thinking season 15" would be the last.

27. Did Carlton Morton look familiar? Well, it's because he's been on an ATL-set reality show before, popping up on The Real Housewives of Atlanta when he was working as Cynthia Bailey's assistant back in 2014. Bravo fans will remember he got into a heated argument with Kenya Moore, who had just joined the series.

28. Why does the show always have those gold cups? While fans have speculated the opaque cups help hide the amount of liquid in the glass to help with editing errors and cuts, Coelen said the goblets were chosen for aesthetics.

"When you turn on the show, you know it's our show," he told Variety. "It's a very authentic, really true following of these people's journeys, but I like the fact that we have this sort of connective tissue with that in a really light way, it's fun."

Deepti added to E! News, "We would always put all of our drinks in the gold goblets. It's just a symbolic thing for us."

#789. Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Bernd Leno (Fulham): Unbelievable couple of saves from him to keep Fulham in the game. I thought Newcastle should have been three or four up before Fulham got the equaliser.

Ronald Araujo (Liverpool): He is just the difference maker to that Liverpool backline. The injury-time Crystal Palace penalty that denied them a clean sheet was a terrible decision, but when he is in the team, they play better and look more solid.

Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest): Exceptional. His goal helps, but exceptional at sniffing out the danger. Erling Haaland didn't have a sniff of a goal in Man City's defeat by Forest. Cunha will need to be really good going forward if they're the team Oliver Glasner wants.

Tarik Muharemovic (Leeds United): Many times he got caught one v one against Spurs but showed his ability to be chilled and calm under pressure and make his tackle. Very unassuming.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was excellent again. He forced Chelsea to go wide and I think that was the key to them winning the game.

Leon Goretzka (Aston Villa): Although it was 4-4 in the end at Man Utd, Goretzka was a beast. He was calm under pressure and moved the ball really well as well. He obviously got a goal but his passing, movement and the ability to just be calm and handle every situation presented to him was really, really good.

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool): How this guy has not got a new deal I don't know. He keeps coming up big, high energy and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play. When he is fit and available and firing on all cylinders it feels like they have a chance in this title race.

Enzo Le Fee (Sunderland): Where would Sunderland be without this guy? He has been good, he has been scoring, chipping in with big moments. Also his ability to take the ball when under pressure, take his side up the pitch and also have that little bit of innovative play and free thinking. He is exceptional.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (Everton): Bossed the game for Everton against Coventry. Unbelievable goal but he absolutely bossed it. There was nothing more he could have done. Never gave the ball away, defensively he was solid. Attacking wise - goals and assists.

Thierno Barry (Everton): The two up front pick themselves, but probably the last time I would have them together in the same team. Did really well, two good goals against Coventry and probably should have had a third as well.

Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest): What a game for him and moment he needed. A lot of pressure from the outside, including myself. Hasn't shown up big this season but against his former team Man City, his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca as well, and he turned around and said, 'you know what, I am the man and you should have kept me around'. Scored two unbelievable goals, led the line well and looked physically fitter and stronger. Maybe now that confidence comes through and we see the best of him after the international break.

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal): I am going for Mikel Arteta simply because he has just won the Premier League. Well done. I said at the start of the season that, for me, Arsenal will win the league by 10 points and this weekend they did it. It's November and the season is officially over.
